summary: Peter Gaeffke was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at PTH Regensburg, under Ernst Schwarz at Mainz (PhD 1952), and at DIAS. He held posts at Utrecht University (professor 1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1972; professor 1975–2003).

Peter Giles was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1878–1882) and Gonville and Caius College (~1882–1887). He served as Reader in Comparative Philology at Cambridge (~1891–1935) and Master of Emmanuel College (~1911–1935).

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his Ph.D. at Yale University. He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1964–1968), Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang with several traditional teachers and earned a PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (attested 2010).
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University from 1975 to 1978. He held a post at SOAS University of London from ~2002 to 2018.
Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1989–1993). He held posts at the University of Giessen (~1994–2002), the University of Düsseldorf (~2002–2004), and the University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He held posts at Brown University (2006–2009) and the Sanskrit Library (President attested 2014; attested 2024–2025).
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tufts University and earned his PhD at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Charles F. Keyes, as well as with several traditional teachers.

Peter N. Gregory is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at Harvard (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1986–1994) and Smith College (attested 2005).
Peter Peterson was an Indologist. Between ~1873 and 1899, he held posts as Professor at the University of Mumbai and as Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College.

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (~1968–1972) and habilitated at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (professor 1990; emeritus ~2010).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his doctorate (~1973–1982) and habilitation (~1982–1995) under Dieter Schuh at the University of Bonn. He held a guest professorship at Humboldt University (2001) and the Tibetology chair at Bonn (2001).

Peter Skilling is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub at the EPHE (2004). He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and taught at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and Pune University.

Peter Stewart is an art and archaeology scholar who completed his MA, MPhil, and PhD at Clare College, Cambridge (~1989–1998). He held posts at Cambridge, Reading, the Courtauld Institute, and Oxford (Associate Professor and CARC from 2011).

Peter Zieme is a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhism who studied at Humboldt University (1960–1965). He served at the GDR Academy (1965–2007), BBAW (~1992–2007), and as an honorary professor at FU Berlin (~2000).
